liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cold Rain And Snow** (1 review): The show opens with a blazing Cold Rain and Snow [10]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): A fan-compiled track list takes Big Railroad Blues from this 4/5/71 Manhattan Center show, mixed with other April 1971 shows [15]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The jam at the end of China Cat flowing into I Know You Rider makes the reviewer doubt it matches the LP [8]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 other source): Not Fade Away and Goin' Down The Road Feelin' Bad appear on the Skull & Roses album [2]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Pigpen is in rare form on King Bee and Lovelight [10]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.miller.110127.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.cantor.gmb.96269.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 174 min; rated 4.71/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.orf.117.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 168 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [5]
- **gd1971-04-05.partial.aud.berger.100052.flac16**: audience recording; 16 songs; 91 min [7]. Said about its sound: Partial audience tape: most songs miss opening notes, and loud passages are severely clipped, suggesting automatic level control or a limiter [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer links the show to an early-70s underground live LP, 'Ain't It Crazy', which opened with The Rub and had China Cat on side two [8]
- Reviewer calls the second set one of the best of 1971, with standout work from Pigpen and Jerry [9]
- Truckin' into The Other One has the intensity and color of 1969; the Dead played hard in NYC in 1970-71 [10]
- Reviewer says this Not Fade Away is not the Skull & Roses one; both Jerry's and Bob's vocals differ [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.miller.110127.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) [1]
- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.cantor.gmb.96269.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: 7" two track reel @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) PCM501ES analog out > dolby A decoder > analog in PCMF1 > analog out > Fostex D5 Dat @ 48 kHz [2]. Also: Cuts in The Other One and Lovelight remain, edited by removing tape squeeze; reel-change dropouts were crossfaded elsewhere [2]
- **gd1971-04-05.sbd.orf.117.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf [5]. Also: Source credits Leigh Orf for sharing this soundboard transfer of the April 1971 show; Leigh Orf digitally remastered the original wav files, removing a 7-8 kHz tone and smoothing reel-flip fades [5][19]
- **gd1971-04-05.partial.aud.berger.100052.flac16**: transferred by Rob Berger; source: aud of unknown origin lineage [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Pandora: [Not Fade Away / Goin' down the Road Feeling Bad (Live at Manhattan Center, New York, NY, April 5, 1971)](https://www.pandora.com/artist/grateful-dead/grateful-dead-skull-and-roses-live/not-fade-away-goin-down-the-road-feeling-bad-live-at-manhattan-center-new-york-ny-april-5-1971/TR3KzvJtpk4Jvg4) [21]
